A positive sentiment analysis (PSA) is an algorithmic process for determining whether or not text contains sentiments such as positivity , negativity , neutrality . The term "sentiment" refers to any emotion expressed in language; thus PSA can be used with both subjective opinions ("I love this movie") and objective facts (“The sun rises every morning”). In contrast to opinion mining algorithms which focus only upon subjectivity, PSAs also analyze objectiveness .
Positive Sentiments
Sentences containing words like “good”, “great” etc., indicate POSITIVE SENTIMENTS while sentences having negative terms like ‘bad’, 'terrible' express NEGATIVE SENTIMENTs. Neutral statements do neither convey strong feelings nor emotions towards something but rather describe things objectively without expressing personal views about them e.g.: He was very happy when he got married.; It rained heavily yesterday afternoon..
Negative Sentiments
Words indicating dislike include: bad, terrible, awful…etc.. Negative phrases may contain adjectives describing unpleasant experiences ('It's so cold outside'), verbs denoting actions performed by others against oneself('They hurt me')or nouns referring directly back at themselves(‘My life has been miserable lately’). These types will usually appear within longer paragraphs where there’s more room available than just one sentence alone!
Neutral Statements
These kinds don't necessarily mean anything specific - they simply state what happened without adding their own interpretation onto those events i.e.'He went shopping today'. This type tends toward shorter passages since most people tend prefer brevity over verbosity anyway!
